name: Carlos Alcaraz

observed.title: Carlos Alcaraz vs Casper Ruud Court-Level Highlights | Paris 2026
observed.camera: court-level, behind the near player (players large and sharp)

observed.title: Carlos Alcaraz vs Ben Shelton Title Battle | Paris 2026 Final Highlights
observed.camera: broadcast (high, wide) plus close-ups between points

outfit.shirt: #1c2340 navy, short sleeves, yellow collar trim
accessories: black wristband on the left wrist

appearance.hair: dark brown, thick and curly, medium length
appearance.headwear: none in Paris (no white hairband here, unlike the long-band look in ROSTER)

forehand.stance: open stance on wide balls, very low (deep knee bend, back knee near the court)
forehand.contact: in front, from a low base
forehand.finish: long, wraps across the body over the left shoulder; back leg kicks up and around on the hard ones
forehand.legs: explosive push from the outside leg, often off the ground at the finish

backhand.stance: open or semi-open on the run, wide base
backhand.takeback: high: racket head up behind the left shoulder, then a loop down
backhand.finish: high over the right shoulder, both hands still on the grip

running.firstStep: explosive crossover into a huge first stride; the back leg stays fully stretched behind
running.braking: plants low on the outside leg and hits from the lunge, then side-shuffles back
running.recovery: quick side shuffle to the centre, small steps

mannerisms: clenched fist toward his box after a winner (v1 65.0, v2 148.0)

gameHints.player-artist: Paris kit: navy shirt with a yellow collar, neon-yellow shorts, black shoes, dark curls; no hairband for this event. Exaggerate the low base and the curls.
gameHints.racket-coach: Backhand: high takeback (racket head up behind the left shoulder), finish high over the right shoulder. Forehand: wrap finish over the left shoulder.
gameHints.animator: Very low centre of mass; open-stance lunge forehand with the back leg flung up; crossover first step with full back-leg extension; recover with a side shuffle.

notSeen: a clear forehand takeback (only finishes and lunges were sharp)
